title: Cause, reason, purpose and result
about: Rather formal ways to say why something happens, why people do things and what happens as a result: due to, owing to, give rise to, with a view to, on the grounds that, consequently, result in and more.

parts.title: Reasons for and purposes of doing things
What comes after the linker
parts.note: Багато зв'язок цього юніту означають майже те саме, тому обирай за тим, що стоїть після них: іменник, ціле речення з дієсловом, -ing чи інфінітив. Головна пастка: owing to і due to — з іменником або -ing, але не з реченням. Якщо далі речення з дієсловом, додай the fact that: Owing to the fact that it was snowing… (а не Owing to it was snowing…). Після with a view to і with the aim of — форма -ing, а не інфінітив. Рядки з because, so as to, in order that тут для порівняння: ти їх уже знаєш.

rows: due to · owing to · because of
a noun
Owing to the fog, our flight was late.
owing to the fact that · due to the fact that
a clause
Owing to the fact that it was foggy, our flight was late.
because · since · as
a clause
As it was foggy, our flight was late.
as a result of · as a consequence of
a noun
Our flight was late as a result of the fog.
as a result · as a consequence · consequently
a comma and a new clause
It was foggy. As a result, our flight was late.
on the grounds that
a clause
They closed the airport on the grounds that it wasn't safe.
with the aim of · with a view to
-ing
We left early with the aim of avoiding the traffic.
in order to · so as to
an infinitive
We left early so as to avoid the traffic.
so that · in order that
a clause
We left early so that we could avoid the traffic.
lead to · result in · give rise to
a noun or -ing
The fog led to long delays.

items.pattern: be due to + noun · due to the fact that + clause
items.meaning: caused by; because of
items.example: Our train was half an hour late **due to** a problem with the signals.
more: The school was closed for two days **due to** heavy snow.
Most of the delay was **due to** roadworks on the motorway.
items.watchOut: «Через» у значенні причини — due to, а не through чи across. Due to + іменник; якщо далі речення з дієсловом — due to the fact that. Не плутай з be due — «очікується»: The train is due at six.

items.pattern: be caused by + noun
items.meaning: happen because of something
items.example: The damp in the bathroom **is caused by** a leaking pipe behind the wall.
more: The fire **was caused by** a candle someone forgot to blow out.
A lot of back pain **is caused by** sitting badly at a desk.
items.watchOut: Спричинений чимось — caused by, а не caused from чи caused with.

items.pattern: the cause of + noun · a common cause of
items.meaning: the thing that makes something happen
items.example: **The cause of** the flood was a burst pipe in the flat upstairs.
more: Doctors still don't know **the cause of** her headaches.
Too much salt is a common **cause of** high blood pressure.
items.watchOut: Причина чогось: the cause of, але the reason for. Не кажи the reason of.

items.pattern: cause sb/sth to + infinitive
items.meaning: make something happen to someone or something
items.example: The smell of burnt toast **caused** the smoke alarm **to go off**.
more: A power cut **caused** all the clocks in the house **to stop**.
The hot weather **caused** the chocolate in my bag **to melt**.
items.watchOut: «Призвело до того, що спрацювала сигналізація» — caused the alarm to go off. Не caused that the alarm went off і не made the alarm to go off (після make інфінітив без to).

items.pattern: owing to + noun · owing to the fact that + clause
items.meaning: because of; rather formal
items.example: **Owing to** the bad weather, the outdoor concert has been cancelled.
more: **Owing to the fact that** the shop was closed, we had to go to the one in town.
Flights are delayed **owing to** fog at the airport.
items.watchOut: Owing to + іменник: owing to the rain. З реченням — owing to the fact that: owing to the fact that it was raining. Після be краще due to: The delay was due to fog. Вимова /ˈəʊɪŋ/ — «оуїнг», не «ауїнг».

items.pattern: spark (off) + noun (protests, a row, complaints)
items.meaning: cause a sudden strong reaction, such as protests or a row
items.example: The plan to close the village school **sparked off** angry protests from parents.
more: A single comment at dinner **sparked off** a huge family row.
The news that the park would be sold **sparked** a petition with 3,000 signatures.

items.pattern: give rise to + noun (gave, given)
items.meaning: cause something to start, often problems, worries or feelings
items.example: The new parking rules have **given rise to** arguments between neighbours.
more: The long hot summer **gave rise to** water shortages in the south.
His strange behaviour **gave rise to** all kinds of rumours in the office.
items.watchOut: Give rise to — без артикля. Give somebody a rise — це «підвищити зарплату».

items.pattern: provoke + noun (a reaction, criticism) · provoke sb
items.meaning: cause a reaction, especially anger or criticism; also annoy someone on purpose
items.example: The decision to raise ticket prices **provoked** an angry reaction from fans.
more: Her post about the neighbours **provoked** a heated discussion online.
The referee's decision **provoked** loud boos from the crowd.

items.pattern: generate + noun (interest, income, criticism)
items.meaning: produce or create something
items.example: The new cycle path has **generated** a lot of interest among local families.
more: The summer festival **generates** a lot of income for the town.
The plans for a new supermarket have **generated** mixed feelings in the village.

items.pattern: bring about + noun (change)
items.meaning: make something, especially a change, happen
items.example: Getting a dog **brought about** a big change in our daily routine.
more: Small daily habits can **bring about** big improvements in your health.
The parents' campaign finally **brought about** a safer crossing outside the school.
items.watchOut: Bring about — спричинити (зміни). Не плутай з bring up — виховувати або піднімати тему.

items.pattern: lead to + noun / -ing (led, led)
items.meaning: cause something to happen later, as a result
items.example: Eating too much sugar can **lead to** serious health problems.
more: A small misunderstanding **led to** a big argument between the two sisters.
The heavy rain **led to** flooding in several streets.
items.watchOut: Lead – led – led (не leaded). Після lead to — іменник або -ing, а не речення: led to an argument, не led to that we argued.

items.pattern: stem from + noun / the fact that
items.meaning: have its origin in; be the direct result of
items.example: A lot of his anxiety **stems from** a bad experience at school.
more: Most of our money problems **stem from** the fact that we never plan ahead.
Most complaints about the hotel **stemmed from** the noisy building work next door.

items.pattern: arise from / out of + noun (arose, arisen)
items.meaning: start or appear as a result of something
items.example: The argument **arose out of** a silly joke about her cooking.
more: Many accidents at home **arise from** carelessness.
Several complaints have **arisen from** the new bin collection times.
items.watchOut: Arise – arose – arisen, не arised. Не плутай з raise (піднімати щось) і rise (підніматися).

items.pattern: sb's reason for (not) doing sth · the reason for sth
items.meaning: why someone does something or why something happens
items.example: Our main **reason for** choosing this flat was the big sunny kitchen.
more: What's the **reason for** the delay?
Her **reason for** moving was to be closer to her parents.
items.watchOut: Причина чогось — reason for, не reason of: my reason for leaving.

items.pattern: the reason (why) + clause … is / was that + clause
items.meaning: used to explain why something happened; less formal
items.uk: причина, чому…; річ у тім, що…
items.example: **The reason why** I'm late is that my bus didn't turn up.
more: **The reason** the café closed was that the rent went up.
I don't know **the reason why** they sold the house.
items.watchOut: «Причина в тому, що…» — The reason is that…, а не The reason is in that…. У формальному тексті краще is that, ніж is because.

items.pattern: sb's motives in / for doing sth
items.meaning: the real, often hidden, reason why someone does something
items.example: Nobody could understand his **motives** in selling the family home so cheaply.
more: Her **motive** for moving abroad was simple: she wanted an adventure.
I'm not sure his **motives** are entirely honest.
items.watchOut: Наголос на перший склад: /ˈməʊtɪv/. Motive часто натякає на приховану причину: What was his real motive?

items.pattern: prompt sb to + infinitive
items.meaning: make someone decide to do something
items.example: What **prompted** you to take up running?
more: A bad back **prompted** her to buy a new mattress.
The rise in bus fares **prompted** many people to start cycling to work.
items.watchOut: Prompt sb to do sth — з to. А make sb do sth — без to: made me leave, але prompted me to leave.

items.pattern: with the aim of + -ing
items.meaning: in order to achieve something
items.example: She joined a choir **with the aim of** making new friends.
more: The council planted more trees **with the aim of** making the town greener.
We're cutting back on takeaways **with the aim of** saving for a holiday.
items.watchOut: «З метою» — with the aim of + -ing: with the aim of saving money. Не for the aim of.

items.pattern: with a view to + -ing
items.meaning: with the plan or hope of doing something later; a bit less direct than with the aim of
items.example: We're looking at houses in the area **with a view to** moving next year.
more: He's learning Spanish **with a view to** living in Spain when he retires.
They bought the old barn **with a view to** turning it into a holiday home.
items.watchOut: Тут to — прийменник, тому далі -ing: with a view to buying, не with a view to buy. Не плутай з in view of — «з огляду на».

items.pattern: on the grounds that + clause · on the grounds of + noun
items.meaning: giving this as the (official) reason
items.example: The landlord kept our deposit **on the grounds that** we had damaged the carpet.
more: She turned down the job **on the grounds that** the hours were too long.
He was refused a ticket **on the grounds of** age.
items.watchOut: Grounds — завжди у множині: on the grounds that. On the ground — «на землі».

items.pattern: the purpose of sth is to + infinitive
items.meaning: what something is for; what it should achieve
items.example: **The purpose of** the meeting is to plan the school summer fair.
more: What's **the purpose of** all these questions?
**The purpose of** my trip to Leeds was to help my sister move house.
items.watchOut: Мета чогось — the purpose of sth is to do sth. On purpose — це «навмисно»: He did it on purpose.

items.pattern: As a result, + clause · as a result of + noun
items.meaning: because of what has just been said
items.example: I forgot to set my alarm. **As a result**, I missed the first train.
more: The road was closed **as a result of** the flooding.
She trained every day and, **as a result**, she finished the marathon in under four hours.
items.watchOut: «В результаті» — as a result, не in the result. Перед іменником — as a result of: as a result of the storm.

items.pattern: As a consequence, + clause · as a consequence of + noun
items.meaning: as a result (more formal)
items.example: He didn't pay his bills for months. **As a consequence**, his electricity was cut off.
more: **As a consequence of** the strike, all flights to Paris were cancelled.
The river burst its banks and, **as a consequence**, hundreds of homes were flooded.

items.pattern: Consequently, + clause · and consequently
items.meaning: so; as a result (formal)
items.example: The bridge was closed for repairs. **Consequently**, we had to take a long detour.
more: She'd never driven in snow and was **consequently** very nervous.
Prices have gone up sharply, and **consequently** fewer families are going abroad this summer.
items.watchOut: Consequently — «отже, внаслідок цього», а не «послідовно» (це consistently). Наголос на перший склад: /ˈkɒnsɪkwəntli/.

items.phrase: the result / consequence of … is that
items.pattern: the result / consequence of sth is that + clause
items.meaning: introduces what has happened because of something
items.example: **The result of** the long dry summer **was that** the garden turned brown.
more: One **consequence of** working from home is that I hardly see anyone during the week.
**The result of** all the roadworks is that the bus takes twice as long.
items.watchOut: «Результат у тому, що…» — The result is that…, без in.

items.pattern: result in + noun / -ing · result from (the other way round)
items.meaning: cause a particular situation; end in it
items.example: His careless driving **resulted in** a serious accident.
more: The storm **resulted in** hundreds of homes losing power.
Skipping breakfast often **results in** snacking later in the day.
items.watchOut: «Призвести до» — result in, не result to. Result from — навпаки, «бути наслідком»: The flood resulted from heavy rain.

items.pattern: the outcome of sth
items.meaning: the final result of a process, meeting, talks or event
items.example: We're still waiting to hear the **outcome** of my brother's job interview.
more: Both families were happy with the **outcome** of the discussion.
The **outcome** of the talks will be announced tomorrow.

items.pattern: the upshot (of sth) was that + clause
items.meaning: the final result (less formal than outcome)
items.example: We argued for an hour about where to go, and **the upshot** was that we stayed at home.
more: The **upshot** of our chat with the neighbours is that they'll cut the hedge every spring.
The **upshot** is that we'll need to find a new babysitter.

items.pattern: chaos / an argument ensued · the ensuing + noun
items.meaning: happen next, as a result (very formal)
items.example: A long argument **ensued** about who should pay for the broken window.
more: The lights went out in the middle of the wedding speech, and total confusion **ensued**.
In the **ensuing** chaos, I lost my phone.
items.watchOut: Ensue не має додатка: chaos ensued, а не The news ensued chaos. Звучить дуже формально; у розмові кажуть followed.

warmup.explain: «Через» у значенні причини — due to (або owing to, because of). Across і via — «через» про простір і маршрут.

warmup.q: The ___ of the fire was old wiring.
warmup.explain: Причина чогось — the cause of. Reason вживають з for: the reason for the fire.

warmup.uk: Через те, що мій телефон розрядився, я не зміг тобі подзвонити.
warmup.q: ___ my phone was dead, I couldn't call you.
warmup.explain: Owing to + іменник. Якщо далі ціле речення з дієсловом, додай the fact that.

warmup.uk: Ця помилка призвела до великої сварки.
warmup.explain: Призвести до — lead to (led to) або result in. Result to і bring to — помилки.

warmup.uk: Ми робимо ремонт у квартирі з наміром її продати.
warmup.q: We're doing up the flat with a view to ___ it.
warmup.explain: With a view to + -ing: тут to — прийменник, а не частка інфінітива.

warmup.uk: Нам не здали квартиру на тій підставі, що в нас є собака.
warmup.q: They wouldn't rent us the flat ___ that we had a dog.
warmup.explain: На тій підставі, що — on the grounds that (grounds у множині). On the ground — «на землі».

warmup.uk: Я проспав і, як наслідок, запізнився на потяг.
warmup.q: I overslept and was ___ late for the train.
warmup.explain: Consequently — отже, внаслідок цього. Consistently — послідовно, постійно; consequent — прикметник.

warmup.uk: Помилка в замовленні призвела до того, що нам привезли два дивани.
warmup.q: A mistake with the order ___ us getting two sofas.
warmup.explain: Result in — призвести до. Result from — навпаки, бути наслідком чогось.

A.q: The ___ of the leak was a loose pipe under the bath.
A.explain: Причина чогось — the cause of. Reason вживають з for, а aim — це мета.

A.q: The sudden noise caused the horse ___.
A.explain: Cause sb/sth to do sth — після cause потрібен інфінітив з to.

A.q: Joining a gym has ___ a real change in my energy levels.
A.explain: Bring about + іменник без прийменника. Led і resulted потребують прийменника: led to, resulted in.

B.q: What was the reason ___ the cancellation?
B.explain: Reason for sth — причина чогось. Не reason of.

B.q: The ___ of my call is to book a table for Saturday.
B.explain: Мета — the purpose of… is to… Reason потребує for, а cause — це причина, а не мета.

B.q: The school started a breakfast club with the aim ___ helping working parents.
B.explain: With the aim of + -ing — з метою.

C.q: Leaving the gate open resulted ___ the dog running away.
C.explain: Result in — призвести до; result from — бути наслідком чогось. «Призвести до» — не result to.

C.q: We'll find out the ___ of the vote on Monday.
The shop put its prices up. ___, it lost a lot of customers.
C.explain: Consequently (отже) стоїть на початку нового речення з комою. Після owing to і with a view to потрібен іменник або -ing.

example.title: The bus that never came
example.uk:
Минулого понеділка автобус о 7:40 так і не приїхав. Причина була в тому, що водій захворів, але нам ніхто не сказав. Через це пів села запізнилося на роботу.

Скасування рейсу викликало десятки гнівних дописів у групі села. Пані Гілл зателефонувала до автобусної компанії, щоб отримати нормальну відповідь. Їй сказали, що проблема виникла через брак водіїв.

У підсумку в шкільній залі скликали громадські збори. Метою зборів було знайти рішення. Після двох годин крику результат виявився простим: компанія погодилася додати ще один ранній рейс. Тож тепер я встигаю на роботу вчасно.
example.en:
Last Monday the 7.40 bus never came. [[The reason|b2]] was that the driver was ill, but nobody had told us. [[As a result|c1]], half the village was late for work.

The cancellation [[sparked off|a6]] dozens of angry posts in the village group. Mrs Hill phoned the bus company [[with the aim of|b5]] getting a proper answer. They told her that the problem [[stemmed from|a12]] a shortage of drivers.

[[The upshot|c7]] was a public meeting in the school hall. [[The purpose of|b8]] the meeting was to find a solution. After two hours of shouting, the [[outcome|c6]] was simple: the company agreed to add an extra early bus. [[Consequently|c3]], I can now get to work on time.
